title: Context Engineering: Connecting the Dots with Graphs — Stephen Chin, Neo4j
talk_summary: Stephen Chin frames context engineering as curating relevant memory and retrieval rather than just writing longer prompts, and demos Neo4j knowledge graphs, GraphRAG, and graph memory. The concrete mechanisms are vector-seeded graph expansion, schema-aware agent traversal through an MCP server, and temporal entity/relationship memory.

takeaways.what_they_do: Use a vector similarity search to find seed nodes, then expand to related nodes and pass that neighborhood as context to the LLM.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The first pass it's going to do a vector lookup and find a similarity search to find related nodes

takeaways.technique: Schema-first agentic graph traversal via MCP
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose the graph schema and query tools to an agent; the agent first reads the schema, then fires multiple queries/traversals and pulls text chunks as needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: first it gets back the schema of the graph so it can understand the relationships

takeaways.what_they_do: Store entities and relationships with text, embeddings, time, and location properties; retrieve via vector search plus graph algorithms like kNN/community/PageRank.
takeaways.evidence_quote: some nodes have the relevant properties such as text details embeddings time and location

takeaways.technique: Suppress tool-output bloat in short-term memory
takeaways.what_they_do: Avoid feeding too much previous tool output into the context window; compress or limit tool results so they do not crowd out relevant context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: not give it too much information from tools... fill our context window

takeaways.technique: Use graphs only for multi-hop relationships
takeaways.what_they_do: Use standard vector RAG for single-shot similarity lookups; use graph retrieval when the answer requires two or more related facts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's where the relationships are two or more where you get the real value
